components.gap: Supply the source's worked normal-form examples and the claims attached to the normal forms (pp. 166, 168-169): in L1 the minimal normal forms of P(a) and Q(a), and the minimal and maximal normal forms of P(a), of P(a)>Q(a), of a formally true and of a formally false sentence; in L2 the 128-member minimal normal forms of P(a) and Q(a); the illustration m_U = 2, 1, 0, 4 (m = 4) of m_U + l_U = m; the source's remark that a minimal sentence has consequences that are neither formally true nor singular, witnessed by (Ex)(P(x)vQ(x)) from P(a)vQ(a); content exclusivity in the source's form (no two minimal sentences share any consequence, of any form, that is not formally true); and the source's justification that the minimal normal form indicates content (minimal, mutually exclusive components) while the maximal normal form indicates range, listing the possible states of the world (each maximal sentence describing one such state as completely as L allows) that would make the sentence true, with the pointer of n. 37 to Carnap's treatment of range and content. The theorem and its complete annex proof state only the general result, restricted to singular consequences.

components.gap: Supply the source's own account of the choice of range measure that this entry illustrates (pp. 170-171, nn. 39-40): that, as Carnap showed ([Inductive Logic] pp. 80-81), the uniform range measure r1 gives the logical probability p1 characteristics incompatible with the intended meaning of logical probability, and that Carnap and Helmer jointly with Hempel and Oppenheim proposed alternative range measures for that reason; and note 40's account of the Helmer-Hempel-Oppenheim alternative: a range measure r_I determined only relative to a sentence I stating the available empirical information, a degree of confirmation dc that is undefined in certain cases with generalized S (McKinsey's review) and does not satisfy all theorems of elementary probability theory, its methodologically desirable features, and the suggestion, left unpursued, of constructing a related systematic-power concept from r_I. The entry instead disclaims any link to Carnap's measure; the route records only the limiting extension, the dependence of dc on empirical information and 'not a probability in the strict sense'. The entry's own two worked range choices and their proofs are complete.
